proxy_language: Proto-Indo-European (late/dialectal, via Proto-Germanic reconstruction as the regional phonological template), with an explicit pre-Indo-European substrate caveat
proxy_rationale: Fosna-Hensbacka (c. 10,000-8,000 BCE) is a Preboreal pioneer maritime hunter-gatherer culture on the Norwegian and Swedish W coast, known only from lithics and coastal sites. Its language is unrecoverable and almost certainly not Indo-European: IE speakers reached Scandinavia only c. 2800 BCE (Corded Ware/Battle Axe). The region's later languages (Proto-Germanic, Sami with its non-Uralic substrate, Finnic) are all intrusive. No attested or reconstructable proto-language exists for these people. The most defensible practical proxy for a name builder is a deliberately archaic, Proto-Germanic/Proto-Indo-European-shaped phonology for the region's coastal, ice-edge ecology, flagged as a placeholder. A pre-IE 'Nordic substrate' would be unknown (cf. Kuhn's Nordwestblock and Sami substrate hypotheses, which are contested). Do not treat any output as the real language of the culture.
phonology: Proxy (late PIE / early Proto-Germanic style): stops *p *t *k *kʷ *b *d *g *gʷ (PIE) shifted by Grimm's law in PGmc to *f *þ *h *hw / *p *t *k; fricatives *s *z *f *þ *h; nasals *m *n; liquids *l *r; glides *w *j. Vowels: short *a *e *i *o *u, long *ā *ē *ī *ō *ū; diphthongs *ai *au *eu. Use a restricted, phonologically plain inventory of 3-5 vowels and common consonants for a 'pioneer' feel. No attested data for the real language.
phonotactics: Proxy templates (C)(C)V(C)(C): open and closed syllables, onset clusters limited to s+stop and stop+liquid (sk-, st-, sp-, tr-, kr-, fl-, sl-), codas up to two consonants (-nt, -rk, -st, -lk). Words are typically 1-3 syllables with initial stress (Germanic style); final obstruents are allowed. No tones. For the audit, avoid CCC onsets and vowel hiatus.
orthography: Plain Latin, reconstruction-style transliteration without asterisks in game names: a e i o u (macrons ā ē ī ō ū optional), b d g p t k s h f þ→'th', m n l r w j→'y'. Use 'k' for /k/, 'th' for /θ/, 'w' for /w/, 'y' for /j/. No c, q, x, z. Avoid the existing game strings' CV-CV 'yusu/momsi' look-alike pattern, which has no linguistic basis.
morphology: Proxy: PIE/PGmc-style roots (CVC) plus thematic vowel and suffixes. Nouns: stem + thematic -a/-o- or -i- or -u-, case endings omitted in names (bare stem or nominative). Common derivational suffixes: -ō(n) agent/weak noun, -ilo diminutive, -ingaz 'descendant/belonging to', -ithō/-ithā abstract. Adjectives follow the noun's stem with an -a- or -i- thematic vowel. Reduplication is rare and is not recommended for the proxy.
compounding: Germanic-style compounding: determinant (modifier) first, head last, joined by a stem vowel or directly (e.g. sea-fish, stone-edge). 'X of Y' is rendered as Y-X compound or as Y-genitive (-as/-is) + X when a phrase is wanted; 'Y-maker' as Y-stem + agent noun (e.g. -smithō, -wrihtaz). Linker vowel -a-/-i- optional in the PGmc style.
noun_phrase_order: Adjective + noun (Germanic/IE usual); genitive before head noun in compounds, either order in phrases. Demonstrative first. For pioneer-culture names prefer simple compounds of 2 morphemes.

worked_examples.name: Stainaþurs
worked_examples.gloss: stain- 'stone' + þurs- (placeholder head); recommend plain compound stain-ax with a known root

sources: Mallory & Adams, The Oxford Introduction to Proto-Indo-European and the Proto-Indo-European World (2006)
Wiktionary Proto-Indo-European and Proto-Germanic reconstruction pages
Bjerck, 'Colonizing Scandinavia' / Fosna and Hensbacka overviews (various, 2008)
Anthony, The Horse, the Wheel, and Language (2007)
notes: No linguistic data exists for Fosna-Hensbacka speakers; they predate Indo-European arrival in Scandinavia by about 5,000 years, and any proxy is a placeholder chosen for regional continuity and phonological plausibility, not a claim of descent. Treat Proto-Germanic/PIE-looking names as stylised labels only. Reconstructed forms are marked with asterisks in the root list; game names omit asterisks. Forms with uncertain etymology (e.g. *swēl- 'sea') are provisional, and some worked examples use placeholder heads. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since this is not a Goidelic culture.
